Click to expand...
I appreciate the honesty, though, you will not be able to make your project open source since the base code including RPG MZ's core scripts are not open source. You can make your game free, however. The plugins you use may or may not be open source, either.
RPG MV's core scripts are MIT licensed (open source).
Buying a commercial project and modifying it will most likely go against the terms of the game itself so I would avoid that. Playing it and trying to recreate the mechanics (which cannot be copyrighted or trademarked) is fine.
Since you mentioned FF2/3, the best way to go about it is to look at tutorials and similarities that you can recreate in the engine. Understanding logic, flow, and timing of how event commands/code gets executed can really help as well.
In terms of projects, you are better off searching for it yourself online and some plugin developers have sample projects that show off their plugins. There is the 'Tutorial...' option under the Help menu with sample projects.

posts.author: ZombieKidzRule
posts.body:
So, if you are brand new to developing in RPG Maker and have no real coding experience, I think you would be much better off finding a series of YouTube tutorials and recreating those in your own project. There are series by creators that start with the basics and go through advance concepts.
You can easily find them by searching YouTube for "RPG Maker MZ Tutorials" and then selecting a creator that has a series of tutorials. The ones I used were about 4-5 years old, but they are still mostly relevant.
Doing the built-in tutorial is a good start, but you can learn an awful lot by recreating YouTube tutorials, not just watching them.
I don't think you are going to find a game specifically like you want that you can download and open in MZ to see how everything works.
Also, while some people think they will learn better that way, as someone who also started to learn MZ and coding a few years ago (in my early 50s) by using YouTube tutorials, I honestly think that just opening a project and trying to figure out what is happening in the Events is going to be much more confusing than taking a slow, systematic approach to learning the basic concepts and building off them.
HOWEVER, in the spirit of trying to help a fellow Gen Xer on their RPG Maker journey, feel free to download and take a look at my only published game that I did for a game jam, Krampus Games. It doesn't have everything I intended to put into it because of the game jam limited time frame. And I'm sure it isn't anything mechanically like the game you want to make.
But, if you think that looking at a project will potentially help you with learning how to use MZ, then feel free. I'm pretty sure I exported my project in a way that makes it so anyone who downloads it can just open the project in their own copy of MZ.
As such, I don't care if anyone wants to recreate anything I did in the project or build off any of the concepts. Especially if they are using it to actually learn and not just doing a quick copy and paste job to avoid the actual hard work of learning the engine. Although, if you do learn something useful and end up using it, I wouldn't mind an honorable mention in your credits some day.
Also, the game isn't anything like your typical RPG Maker game with maps and sprites. It goes in an entirely other direction. Sort of like my current Sudoku game project.
Finally, just a warning, I haven't looked at this project in a long time and I have learned a LOT since I published it. I'm sure that now I would do a lot of things differently.
AND, when I made this project, I don't recall being very good about using Comments in Events to help me (or anyone else who looks at it later) recall what I was doing and why.
I have subsequently learned how very useful Comments are in Events as notes to your future self (or anyone else who looks at your code or project).
As a bonus, I do recall making a few YouTube tutorials about how I did certain things in my game jam project. Those might help a little too if you are looking at the project as just one more tool to help you learn.
Finally, I do have quite a few tutorials on my own YouTube page, but my tutorials don't really cover the basics and sort of assume that you already learned those from other tutorials.
Anyway, here is a link to my Itch.io page. Again, I believe you can just download the zip file, unzip it, and put it in the same place as the other project folders for your MZ. Then you should be able to open the project like you would any other project that you started yourself.
Krampus Games (Game Jam 2023) by ZombieKidzRule
RPGMAKERWEB.COM Game Jam 2023 Entry
zombiekidzrule.itch.io
Good luck and I hope this helps some. If you want to reach out to me, feel free to do so as well.
Take care and remember to enjoy what you do!
